title: Investigation vignettes — microdash metrics and trace guides
body:
Purpose:
This note collects short investigation vignettes that map a specific operational symptom -> minimal metric set -> trace anchors -> microdashboard layout. The goal is a small set of compact diagnostic pages (microdashes) that an on-call engineer can scan in 60–90s and either resolve or get to a reproducible hypothesis.

How to use this doc:
- Each vignette is intentionally compact: symptom, hypotheses, metric checklist (3–6 signals), trace span anchors and a tiny dashboard sketch with example queries/filters.
- If you make a change to an instrumentation signal, update the metric name and a short rationale here.
- Microdashes are built as templated panels in Grafana (or internal microdash service) and should be copied into incident runbooks.

Vignette A — "Long tail token latency (sporadic p99 spikes)"
Symptom:
- Customers report occasional single-request slow responses. Host-level GPU utilization and QPS look fine; only a few requests show high tail latency.
Immediate hypotheses:
1) Cold KV-cache miss cascades for multi-hop sessions.
2) Long-running kernel fallback on some model shard (quantization fallback).
3) Network hiccup between front proxy and serving instance.
Metric checklist (minimal):
- inference.request.latency_ms.histogram (buckets: 1,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000) — histogram to inspect tail shape
- kv_cache.hit_rate (gauge, 0–1) — per-model, per-tenant
- batch.size.p50/p95 (gauge) — higher batch sizes can correlate with spikes
- model.kernel_fallback.count (counter) — increments when a slower kernel is used
- host.net.retransmits_per_min (gauge) — proxy->serving network indicator
Trace anchors and spans to inspect:
- root span: request/serve (attributes: model_name, model_version, tenant_id, request_id, seq_len_input)
- span: kv_cache/lookup (attrs: key_count, hit:Boolean) — look for long durations on misses
- span: kernel/quant_fallback (attrs: kernel_name, device, reason)
- span: network/proxy-forward (attrs: rtt_ms)
Sampling guidance:
- For this vignette prefer severity-weighted sampling biased to requests with latency > p95 and where kv_cache.hit_rate < 0.8. Preserve first 1K tokens of prompt and redact user PII.
Microdash layout (3 rows):
Row 1: quick summary
- Panel: p50/p95/p99 latency timeseries (line) with tenant filter and model filter
- Panel: kv_cache.hit_rate (heatmap by model shard)
Row 2: attribution
- Panel: kernel_fallback.count (bar stacked by kernel_name)
- Panel: batch.size.p95 vs latency scatter
Row 3: traces
- Panel: sample trace list (columns: request_id, latency_ms, kv_hit, kernel_fallback) linking to trace viewer
Example queries (PromQL-like pseudocode):
- p99_latency = histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_name))
- kv_miss_rate = 1 - avg_over_time(kv_cache.hit_rate{model_name=~".*"}[10m])
- kernel_fallback_rate = increase(model_kernel_fallback_count[15m])

Vignette B — "Throughput drop with steady request rate"
Symptom:
- QPS observed from front door is stable, but tokens/sec processed by the pool falls and queueing grows.
Hypotheses:
1) Autoscaler mis-evaluating usable GPU slots (node draining or daemon crash).
2) Background compaction/GC consuming CPU on host leading to decreased host scheduling for batching thread.
3) New model variant deployed with higher per-token latency.
Metric checklist:
- inference.tokens_per_sec (gauge aggregated by pool and by region)
- serving.active_workers (gauge) — number of serving processes accepting work
- host.system.load1 (gauge) and host.cpu_steal_pct (gauge)
- rollout.model_variant_active (gauge, tag by variant)
- queue.request_depth (gauge) — per-pool
Trace anchors:
- span: scheduler/batch_collect (attrs: wait_ms, chosen_batch_size)
- span: worker/process_request (attrs: worker_id, device_free_mem_mb)
- span: orchestrator/scale_decision (attrs: desired_replicas, reason)
Microdash sketch:
Row 1: capacity snapshot (tokens/sec, active_workers, desired_replicas)
Row 2: queueing vs batch sizes (stacked area)
Row 3: recent deployments and variant p95 latency timeline
Quick checks during an incident:
- Are worker counts decreasing? If yes, correlate with node lifecycle events (kube events).
- Is batch_collect wait increasing? If yes, investigate scheduling thread CPU contention.

Vignette C — "Spammy fallback / hallucination surge"
Symptom:
- Sudden rise in fallback_count and downstream user complaints about incoherent outputs.
Hypotheses:
1) Model weight regression introduced by a new quant profile or tokenization mismatch.
2) Prompt pipeline started truncating system messages causing model confusion.
3) Malicious/edge prompt pattern causing hallucination pattern detection to trigger fallbacks unpredictably.
Metric checklist:
- model.fallback.count (counter, tags: variant, tenant)
- eval.hallucination_score.mean (gauge, reference on eval set)
- prompt.length.dist (histogram)
- routing.fallback_reason{reason="quality"/"timeout"/"capacity"} (counter)
Trace anchors:
- span: prompt-normalizer (attrs: truncated:Boolean, truncation_len)
- span: model/inference (attrs: temperature, top_p, quant_profile)
- span: safety/filter (attrs: rule_hits)
Microdash panels:
- waterfall of fallback_count by reason (short window)
- prompt length vs hallucination score scatter grouped by tenant
- sample traces showing full prompt (redacted) and model outputs for manual QA

Metric definition mini-catalog (compact) — use these names in dashboards and alerts
- inference.request.latency_ms.histogram: type=histogram, unit=ms, owner=eng-serving-runtime, use=tail analysis and SLOs
- inference.tokens_per_sec: type=gauge, unit=tokens/s, owner=eng-serving-runtime, use=capacity dashboards
- kv_cache.hit_rate: type=gauge (0..1), unit=ratio, owner=eng-cache, use=caching efficiency and cost attribution
- model.kernel_fallback.count: type=counter, unit=count, owner=eng-runtime, use=detect slow-path regressions
- queue.request_depth: type=gauge, unit=requests, owner=eng-sre, use=backpressure alerts
- rollout.model_variant_active: type=gauge (0/1 per variant), unit=boolean, owner=product-hosted-api, use=canary detection and rollbacks

Tracing guidelines (compact):
- Minimal required attributes on root span: {request_id, tenant_id, model_name, model_version, seq_len_input, client_region}
- Span naming conventions: snake_case and grouped by subsystem: request/serve, kv_cache/lookup, scheduler/batch_collect, kernel/execute, network/proxy_forward, safety/check
- Span durations should be recorded in ms and exposed as metric delta for heavy hitters
- Event annotations: record key events (cache_miss, kernel_fallback, model_fallthrough) as span events — helps filter in trace UI
- Sampling: default tail-sampling window 5m with severity bias (latency > p95, fallback_count > 0, errors). Keep deterministic sampling for tenants flagged as "debug-mode" (sample 100%).
- Privacy: redact prompt contents beyond first 512 characters; apply PII scrubbing rules linked in confluence artifact above.

Dashboard hygiene notes (practical):
- Keep microdash panels to 6–9 short widgets. Each should answer a single question.
- Use multi-dim heatmaps sparingly — prefer a small table if cardinality is large.
- Always include a trace-list panel with prefilled filters matching the metric selection for that page to accelerate jump-to-trace flows.
- Version your microdash template: add a "doc_version" panel text box with the file revision and a short rationale field.
- Cost-aware views: include a small numeric panel for estimated token spend delta per 1k requests (derived from tokens_per_sec and unit cost) when investigating cost regressions.

Operational checklist for adding a new signal:
1) Write a short definition (name, type, owner, unit, cardinality) and add it to the Metric Catalog PR.
2) Add metadata to instrumentation repo (link to PR in linked_artifacts).
3) Add a microdash panel and a short blurb in the runbook vignette.
4) After deploy, run short smoke queries for 24h and look for unexpected zeros or unbounded growth.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Better default thresholds for kv_cache.hit_rate alerts by model family (need historical analysis).
- Automate trace sampling ruleset rollout per-customer for privacy-sensitive tenants.
- Compact serialization format for microdash templates to permit programmatic generation from incident playbooks.

Notes / references:
- Refer to INF-4321 for the prototype microdash backend used in experiments.
- See infra PR #789 for kernel fallback telemetry changes (kernel_name attribute).
- Confluence: signal catalog has canonical types and owners — link included above.

Author notes:
This is intentionally lightweight and biased toward actionable panels for on-call flow. If this format proves useful, we can convert vignettes into a small templating repo and add automatic dashboard generation.

Last edited by: Priya Shukla on 2024-03-10
